sources.quote: GLM-5.3 always operates with reasoning enabled and supports three reasoning effort levels: low, high, and max.
It defaults to `max` if not passed (or if set to any other value).
tool_choice: Controls function calling strategy, default is auto (only supports auto)
This kind of structured task input reduces unnecessary guesswork and makes the agent’s changes more consistent and easier to review.
Do not introduce new dependencies, do not modify API contracts, and do not commit changes proactively.
We find that GLM-5.2 shows more potential hacking behavior than GLM-5.1.
ZCode only reads the user global AGENTS.md and the current Workspace AGENTS.md.
Every agent diff is re-graded on a pristine image, and we publish both grades.
Even the leading LLM, GLM-5.2, fails to follow about 20% of the process constraints
GLM-5.3-Prime is the high-speed variant of Z.ai's GLM-5.3, inheriting its full capabilities while delivering 1.5–2× the output throughput through inference acceleration.

pricing: Z.ai publishes no batch price; OpenRouter lists a separate batch id

released: Z.ai's blog is dated 2026-08-14 (announcement); its release notes and Artificial Analysis give 2026-08-18; the Hugging Face repository was created 2026-08-25; 08-18 is used because it is the API date
active parameters: Z.ai does not state them; Artificial Analysis lists 753B total and 40B active, a vLLM recipe lists about 743B and 39B
system_card: Z.ai publishes no system card or safety report for GLM-5.3; the blog, docs page and Hugging Face card are the whole record
safety evaluations: no published refusal, over-refusal, sycophancy, prompt-injection or classifier results found
